battle.name: 癸酉之變
battle.brief: 嘉慶十八年七月，河南滑縣天理教起義，連動山東曹州與直隸各府；九月十五日夜，數十名教眾潛入北京紫禁城，與內務府護軍激戰於隆宗門一帶，終因彈藥耗盡而潰散。清廷調三省綠營與團練數萬鎮壓，火繩式抬槍與鳥槍是雙方最普遍的遠射手槍。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 大清一方是天理教起義逼出來的中央與直隸、山東、河南三省軍政聯盟。京師宿衛由內務府與步軍營分掌：內務府護軍專司紫禁城與內廷宿衛，內大臣輪值門禁，步軍營分守九門與外城，五營巡捕在街巷往來搜捕。地方上，直隸總督那彥成節制直隸、山東、河南三省綠營與團練，滑縣事發後以失察革職，由顏檢接任；河南方面吳熊光、山東督撫同受嚴責，記載對處分輕重略有出入。剿匪的骨幹是臨時徵集的團練與鄉勇，練總多為地方紳士與生員，練勇自備鳥槍、抬槍、長矛與大刀，府縣出錢糧供應。起義一方沒有國家、沒有軍令系統，天理教在官方檔案裡多稱八卦教或邪教，以香會、吃齋與結拜維繫組織，教首李文成居河南滑縣，山東曹州、直隸大名與廣平一帶的教眾隨之響應，另有一支小隊事先潛入京師準備內應。雙方都沒有外國勢力直接介入這場內亂；值得注意的是同一件火繩槍在西班牙、荷蘭與英國已是步兵制式裝備，傳入中國後卻只落地成零散的鳥槍與抬槍，兩地裝備落差本身就藏在這場內亂的伏線裡。
countriesEn: On the Qing side the war was fought by a coalition of the central government with the officials and troops of Zhili, Shandong and Henan, forced into being by the Tianli rising. The defence of the capital was divided between the Imperial Household Department and the Capital Garrison: the Household banner guards held the Forbidden City and the inner court, the household ministers took turns at the gates, the garrison divisions held the nine gates and the outer city, and patrols of the Five Battalions searched the streets. In the provinces the Viceroy of Zhili, Na Yancheng, exercised command over the Green Standard and the drill units of the three provinces; after the outbreak at Huaxian he was dismissed for failing to detect it, and Yan Jian took over. Wu Xionguang of Henan and the governor of Shandong were held to account in the same way, though the records differ slightly on the severity of the punishments. The backbone of the suppression was the drill militia and the village braves raised on the spot, whose drill leaders were usually local gentry and students, whose men brought their own fowling pieces, shoulder muskets, spears and sabres, and whom the prefectures and counties paid and fed. The insurgents had no state and no command system. The Tianli cult, called the Eight Trigrams cult or heterodox teaching in the official files, was held together by incense meetings, fasting communions and sworn brotherhood; its leader Li Wencheng lived at Huaxian in Henan, followers in Caozhou in Shandong and in Daming and Guangping in Zhili rose in answer, and a separate small party slipped into the capital beforehand to prepare an insurrection from within. No foreign power was directly involved in this civil strife. It is worth noting that the very same matchlock was standard issue in the infantry of Spain, the Netherlands and England, yet in China it had settled only as scattered fowling pieces and shoulder muskets, and that gap between the two hides inside the background of this war.
people: 嘉慶帝是整件事的震央。癸酉年九月他正在熱河木蘭行圍，聞報京師遭襲後連夜馳返，數日抵京，下詔究辦值宿宿衛與三省督撫。皇城內廷一帶，妃嬪與年幼皇子安居其中，起義者始終未能接近，她們的安全全賴內務府護軍與內大臣的應變。當夜迎戰者主要是內務府護軍、內大臣與步軍營城上兵卒，另有巡捕五營在街巷搜索；事後數十名失職的太監、護軍與校尉被究辦，內務府與步軍營的人事為之一變。起義一方的主腦是滑縣教首李文成，起義前以符水、治病聚眾，事起後據滑縣城與清軍相持數月，城破時與家屬自焚殉難，或說他突圍被殺，各說不一。曹州與直隸一帶教首的姓名與事跡諸說並存，不能盡信。潛入京師的小隊有數十人，被俘者僅數人，其中二人被解送京師，姓名有記作陳爽、陳連者，說法不一。地方官方面，那彥成革職、顏檢接任直隸總督，改用重兵圍城的辦法；州縣官員多在失察與通匪之間被究辦，練總與里正被要求具結保甲，連坐之風由此打開。
peopleEn: The Jiaqing Emperor was the centre of the whole affair. In the ninth month of the guiyǒu year he was hunting at Mulan in Jehol; when he heard that the capital had been attacked he rode back by night, reached Peking within days, and at once issued edicts holding the night watch and the provincial governors to account. Inside the inner court the imperial consorts and the infant princes were sitting out the night, the insurgents never came near them, and their safety rested entirely on the Household banner guards and the household ministers who reacted in time. Those who met the attack that night were chiefly the Household banner guards, the household ministers and the garrison soldiers on the walls, with patrol detachments of the Five Battalions searching the streets behind them; afterwards dozens of negligent eunuchs, guards and cadets were brought to account, and the personnel of the Household Department and of the Capital Garrison were reshuffled. The chief of the insurgents was Li Wencheng, the cult leader of Huaxian, who had gathered followers with charms and by healing the sick; once the revolt was under way he held Huaxian city against the imperial troops for several months, and when the city fell he died with his family in the fire, though some accounts say he was killed trying to break out, and the stories differ. The names and deeds of the cult leaders in Caozhou and in Zhili are inconsistently recorded and cannot be taken at face value. The party that slipped into the capital numbered several dozen men, and only a few were taken alive, two of whom were sent to Peking, named as Chen Shuang and Chen Lian in one account, though the names are not certain. Among the officials, Na Yancheng was dismissed and Yan Jian succeeded him as Viceroy of Zhili and adopted a method of heavy encirclement; county and prefectural officers were caught between the charge of failure to detect and the charge of complicity, and drill leaders and village headmen were made to file guarantees for the household registration system, so that a climate of collective liability opened with it.
kits: 火繩槍是這場戰爭裡真正上手的形制，這點必須說清楚。火繩槍是十五世紀末到十六世紀初伊比利亞半島的產物，一五二〇年前後西班牙大方陣的步兵以之為遠射手，槍上帶點火機件，射手先點著預先處理過的慢燃火繩，扣扳機把火星送進火藥盤，再由火藥盤引燃主藥，射速不過每分鐘數發，而且要架住槍身仔細瞄準；它的長處是讓一整排射手同時打出一片彈幕，弱點則集中在點火、夜戰與排隊三處。中國這邊走的正是同一條路。十六世紀葡人據澳門、日本火繩槍經海路與朝貢貿易東來，明代已仿出鳥槍等火器，明末清初又出現架在肩上或以叉架支撐的抬槍；到一八一三年，中方火器的主體仍是火繩式的抬槍與鳥槍，火藥靠北方硝土與內地硫磺供應，鉛料自雲南會澤啟運，往往在路上就耗去數月，軍中常見回收舊彈重澆或以銅片包鐵充數。歐洲方面，西班牙自己的軍隊在一六二〇年代已換上燧發槍，這件一五二〇年的火繩槍在他們那裡早是舊制；在中國，它卻仍是鄉兵手上最常見的傢伙。起義教眾的槍械多出自民間私藏，數量零散，未經統一操練；清軍綠營槍兵比例偏低，團練手上的鳥槍與抬槍也雜亂不堪。冷兵器方面，雙方都大量使用長矛、大刀與弓箭，攻城方用雲梯、穴地與火藥爆破，守方用密集火器配合滾木擂石與拒馬，糧草與彈藥靠衛河、黃河水運加陸路車隊，華北秋雨連綿時道路泥濘，軍需往往比士氣先一步耗盡。
kitsEn: The matchlock is the weapon that was actually in the hands of the men in this war, and that needs to be said plainly. The matchlock was a product of the late fifteenth and early sixteenth century Iberian peninsula; around 1520 the Spanish tercio infantry carried it as their long arm, and the gun had a lock that worked with a burning cord: the soldier lit the slow match, which had been prepared beforehand, pulled the trigger to throw a spark into the priming pan, and the flash from the pan set off the main charge. The rate of fire was a few rounds a minute at best, and the shooter had to rest the musket and aim carefully. Its strength was that it let a whole rank fire at once and lay down a sheet of bullets; its weaknesses were concentrated in lighting the cord, in fighting at night and in holding the line. China had come by exactly the same technology. Portuguese at Macao in the sixteenth century and Japanese matchlocks arriving by sea and through tribute trade carried it east, and the Ming already copied fowling pieces and other matchlock arms, with the shoulder-fired musket, rested on the shoulder or on a forked rest, appearing by the late Ming and early Qing. In 1813 the bulk of Chinese firearms was still the matchlock shoulder musket and fowling piece; powder came from nitre of the north and sulphur from the interior, lead travelled from Huize in Yunnan and had often spent months on the road, and the troops commonly recovered spent bullets for recasting or sheathed iron with copper to make up the shortfall. In Europe the position was the other way round: the Spanish army itself had taken up the flintlock from the 1620s, so a matchlock of 1520 was already an obsolete pattern there, while in China it remained the most common arm in the hands of village soldiers. The guns of the insurgents came out of private caches, were scattered in number and had never been drilled together; in the Green Standard the proportion of gunners was low, and the drill units held an equally jumbled mix of fowling pieces and shoulder muskets. In cold weapons both sides used spears, sabres and bows in bulk. The besiegers used ladders, mines and powder, the defenders answered with close volleys, rolling logs, stones and chevaux-de-frise, and grain and ammunition moved by water on the Wei and Yellow rivers and by wagon on land. When the autumn rains turned the roads of north China to mud, the supply of powder and food wore out before the men did.
tactics: 起義方的打法是典型的秘密結社式攻城。教眾平日分散鄉間，以香會、吃齋與結拜聯絡，事起便在夜裡集結，扮作行商、腳夫或香客進城，先以冷兵器襲擊守門的團練與差役，再用人數壓垮城內守備，奪門後開城迎接城外人馬。據城之後靠築寨、掘壕與拒馬自守，兵員不足時以老弱上城助守。河南滑縣是首義之地，起義軍據城抵抗清軍達數月，並分兵襲擊周邊縣城、斷絕糧道，把戰線拉成廣泛的騷擾網。曹州與直隸的響應者各攻破若干州縣，遇清軍主力即散為游眾，藉地形與村寨游擊。九月十五日夜的皇城突襲是其中最險的一手：數十名教眾事先潛入京師，藏在內城附近街巷，待夜分從宣武門一帶突入，企圖循內廷方向直入。火繩槍在這種夜戰裡最是吃力：起義者只有短槍與冷兵器，火藥與鉛彈攜帶有限，槍口火焰也照亮了自己的身形；天色未明，彈藥便已告罄，餘下的人只能以刀矛在火光中搏鬥。守方自內中出迎，步軍營封閉城門、街巷戒嚴，起義者雖深入至隆宗門一帶，終因無攻門器械而潰散，天明後或被殺或被俘，防守方逐門搜索全城數日。清軍的戰術則是典型的圍城打援：重兵合圍滑縣切斷糧水，要道上設卡查驗往來，斷絕城內外消息；團練分駐各鄉，築寨自守，遇小股起義軍便以槍矛圍殲，遇大股則報官請兵，收復失地多用夜襲奪寨、迫降與斷糧三管齊下，避開硬攻城牆的傷亡。
tacticsEn: The method of the insurgents was the classic secret-society assault on a walled town. In normal times the followers were scattered across the countryside and kept in touch through incense meetings, fasting communions and sworn brotherhood; when the moment came they mustered at night, dressed as pedlars, porters or pilgrims, slipped into the town, first struck the drill guards and constables at the gates with cold weapons, then overwhelmed the garrison by sheer numbers, and once the gate was taken opened it to the men waiting outside. Established in a town they relied on stockades, ditches and chevaux-de-frise, and when their fighting men ran short they put old men and boys on the walls to help. Huaxian in Henan, the first place to rise, held out against the imperial troops for several months; the rebels struck at the surrounding counties, cut the food routes and turned the fighting into a wide harassment. In Caozhou and Zhili the followers who rose in answer took scattered county towns and dissolved into the countryside as soon as a real imperial force came near, fighting as skirmishers from villages and stockades. The night of the fifteenth of the ninth month was the most dangerous card they played: several dozen men had entered the capital beforehand and lay hidden in the streets near the inner city, waiting for the hour of the watch to strike from the direction of Xuanwu Gate and drive straight through to the inner court. The matchlock was at its worst in such a night action. The insurgents had only short guns and cold weapons, they carried limited powder and lead, and the flash of their own muzzles lit up their bodies. Before dawn their ammunition was gone, and what was left of them could only fight with blades and spears in the torchlight. The defenders came out from within, the Capital Garrison shut the gates and put the streets under curfew, and the insurgents, though they reached as far as the Longzong Gate area, broke up for want of siege equipment; by morning they had been killed or taken, and the defenders spent the following days searching the city gate by gate. The Qing method, by contrast, was the classic siege with interceptions: heavy forces ringed Huaxian to cut its food and water while checkpoints on the roads checked travellers and severed all contact with the outside; the drill units were posted in the villages behind their own stockades, surrounded and destroyed small bands of rebels with gunfire and spear, and called for regular troops when faced with a serious rising. The recovery of lost ground relied on night attacks on stockades, on offering terms of surrender, and on cutting food supplies, avoiding the cost of storming the walls head-on.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間線：嘉慶十八年即一八一三年七月，河南滑縣教首李文成起義；其後教眾響應於山東曹州與直隸各府；九月十五日夜，即公曆一八一三年十月八日，起義者突襲紫禁城；十月滑縣城破，李文成死於城破；曹州、直隸一帶據點相繼肅清，至嘉慶十九年即一八一四年初基本平定，前後約一年。皇城之夜，突進者人數各說不一，官方諭旨與後人記述多作五六十人，亦有記數十人者；交戰於隆宗門一帶，起義者除被殺者外僅數人被俘，其中二人被解送京師，姓名有記作陳爽、陳連者，說法不一。兵力：清廷先後調集直隸、山東、河南三省綠營馬步兵數千，另有團練與鄉勇數萬，分散在數百處寨卡與城鎮；起義者沒有固定編制，攻城時可集數千，戰後官方以擒斬數萬計，並稱被裹挾者以數十萬計，這些都是諭旨的措辭，實際數字無法核實。行政代價：事後那彥成革職、顏檢接任直隸總督，河南、山東多名州縣官員被貶調或革職，京師內務府與步軍營一批值宿人員被究辦，並掀起大規模追查教門的案件。距離上，滑縣至京師約六百餘公里，消息與兵力的往來全靠驛馬與步騎，數月之後才能成軍。時間跨度方面，皇城事變到嘉慶帝自熱河返京只隔數日，追緝餘黨的工作一直持續到年底。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The chronology: in the seventh month of Jiaqing's eighteenth year, 1813, Li Wencheng rose at Huaxian in Henan; his followers answered in Caozhou in Shandong and in the prefectures of Zhili; on the night of the fifteenth of the ninth month, which was 8 October 1813 in the western calendar, the insurgents attacked the Forbidden City; in the tenth month Huaxian fell and Li Wencheng died in the ruins; the strongholds in Caozhou and Zhili were then reduced one by one, and by the beginning of Jiaqing's nineteenth year, 1814, the rising was essentially suppressed, a span of about a year. On the numbers at the palace that night the accounts differ; the official edicts and later writers usually give fifty or sixty men, others say only a few dozen. The fighting ran around the Longzong Gate, and apart from those killed the insurgents lost only a few men taken alive, two of whom were sent to Peking, named as Chen Shuang and Chen Lian in one account, though the names are not certain. On strength: the court moved several thousand Green Standard horse and foot from Zhili, Shandong and Henan, with tens of thousands of drill guards and village braves distributed among several hundred stockades, checkpoints and walled towns. The insurgents had no regular establishment; several thousand could be brought together for an assault, and afterwards the official count claimed tens of thousands killed and taken, with hundreds of thousands said to have been dragged in unawares; these are the phrases of the edicts, and the real figures cannot be verified. On the administrative cost: Na Yancheng was dismissed and Yan Jian took over as Viceroy of Zhili, a number of prefectural and county officers in Henan and Shandong were demoted, transferred or dismissed, and a batch of Household and Capital Garrison men on night watch were called to account, which set off a large-scale pursuit of cult cases across the provinces. In distance, Huaxian lies some six hundred kilometres or more from Peking, and men and news travelled by post horse and on foot, so it took months for an army to be assembled. In time, only a few days separate the attack on the palace from the emperor's return from Jehol, and the hunt for the remnants went on to the end of the year.
cause: 起因要分三層說。第一層是長期的鎮壓與地下化：白蓮教一系在明清以來屢遭打壓，到嘉慶朝改以香會、吃齋、結拜等民間形式傳播，教首多由草莽人物、醫者與遊方僧道擔任，信眾以農民、礦工、流民與城鄉手藝人為主。乾隆末至嘉慶初的白蓮教起義被平定之後，教門並未消失，而是轉入更隱蔽的形態，組織與地方械鬥結合，形成所謂教匪與團練互相消耗的局面。第二層是災荒與流動：嘉慶十八年前後直隸、山東、河南一帶乾旱、水災相繼，糧價飛升，災民流徙，教門成為流民最易加入的團體，會眾因此迅速膨脹。第三層是直接導火線：滑縣教首李文成在地方清剿與教內糾紛中被迫提前舉事，起義一旦爆開，山東曹州與直隸各府教眾群起響應，而事前情報未能上達，京師對方滲入者竟無人察覺，這才是皇城之變的直接背景。史觀上要注意，清廷敘事把這類起義一律稱為邪教與匪患，講究剿滅；近年的教派史研究則強調其群眾性、災荒成因與地方社會的對抗結構。兩種敘事對同一批史料的取捨不同，這也是這場戰爭至今仍被重新評價的原因。
causeEn: The causes are best given in three layers. The first is a long history of suppression followed by underground survival: the White Lotus tradition had been beaten down again and again since the Ming, and by the Jiaqing reign it passed on in folk forms such as incense meetings, fasting communions and sworn brotherhood, with local notables, healers and itinerant monks and Taoists serving as cult leaders, and with farmers, miners, vagrants and urban craftsmen as the core of the membership. The White Lotus rising of the late Qianlong and early Jiaqing years had been suppressed, but the cult did not disappear: it went deeper underground, its organisation became entangled with local feuds, and the result was a state of affairs in which cult bandits and drill guards ground each other down. The second layer is famine and displacement: in the years around Jiaqing's eighteenth year, drought and flood struck Zhili, Shandong and Henan in turn, grain prices soared, and the cult was the easiest group for vagrants to join, so the membership swelled quickly. The third layer is the immediate spark: the cult leader at Huaxian, Li Wencheng, was driven into open revolt ahead of schedule by the local crackdown and by disputes inside the cult, and once the rising was under way the followers in Caozhou and in the prefectures of Zhili rose in answer; word of it did not reach the authorities in time, and the men who had slipped into the capital went unnoticed, and that is the direct background to the attack on the palace. On interpretation, it matters that the Qing's own narrative called all such risings heterodox teaching and banditry and was written to justify eradication, whereas recent scholarship on religious sects emphasises the popular character of the movement, the role of famine and the confrontational structure of local society. The two narratives select differently from the same record, and that is why this war is still being reassessed.
impact: 影響可以分近遠兩層。近層是宮禁與地方治理的重整。皇城被突襲在制度上是一次難堪的失敗：內務府與步軍營的宿衛編制、夜巡方式與門禁手續被重新訂立，失職人員遭撤換，皇城各門的警衛與火器配置加強，後宮與內廷侍衛的選任與輪值也收緊；其後更定下門上加鎖、內外城分設警衛、旗籍與漢軍分守的辦法。地方上，督撫因失察受連帶處分，剿匪成為州縣官員的第一考績，連帶引發嚴禁教門、嚴禁民間私藏火器與密集的連坐式查辦，民間因此氣氛緊張，地方官多以多報、嚴辦自保。遠層在兵制：經此一役，團練與鄉勇在河南山東直隸全面制度化，地方武裝化程度大增；二十多年後太平天國戰爭興起時，地方練勇反而成為清廷最難駕馭的力量，湘軍、淮軍正是從這套團練體制裡生長出來並最終坐大。武器層面同樣有後果：民間火器被嚴禁，農村火器水準長期落後，火繩式抬槍繼續充當主力；而軍方對洋槍的需求開始上升，廣州口岸的英製燧發步槍進口量在道光年間明顯增加，這條供應線到鴉片戰爭前已經存在，卻未能改變清軍整體的射擊水準。
impactEn: The effects work on two levels, near and far. In the near term the attempt on the palace was a humiliating institutional failure: the system of night watch, the way patrols were run and the procedure at the gates of the Household Department and of the Capital Garrison were all rewritten, negligent personnel were removed, the guarding and the disposition of firearms at the gates of the Forbidden City were tightened, and the selection and rotation of the inner-court guards were revised; afterwards came the locking of the gates, the posting of separate guards to the inner and outer cities, and the division of the watch between banner and Han troops. In the provinces, the governors and viceroys were punished in succession for failure to detect, the suppression of the cult became the first duty to be weighed in the assessment of county magistrates, and this brought in its wake a severe ban on the sects, a severe ban on private firearms in the hands of the people, and a wave of collective-punishment investigations, so that the atmosphere in the country tightened and most local officers made a practice of reporting numbers high and dealing harshly. In the longer term there was a change in military organisation: after this rising, drill units and village braves were institutionalised throughout Henan, Shandong and Zhili, and the militarisation of the countryside went a long way. When the Taiping rebellion broke out a little more than two decades later, these local forces turned out to be the hardest for the court to control, and the Xiang and Huai armies grew out of this very system of drill militia before growing too strong for it. The weapon question had consequences too: firearms in private hands were banned, rural weapon standards fell behind for a long time, and the matchlock shoulder musket went on serving as the main arm, while the army's demand for imported guns rose, and the number of British flintlock muskets entering through the Canton factories increased noticeably during the Daoguang reign. That supply line already existed before the Opium War, yet it had not changed the general standard of Qing shooting.
result: 結果分軍事、政治與象徵三層。軍事上，清方在半年內平定：滑縣城破後，首義者李文成死於城破，曹州與直隸的響應據點被逐一攻破或迫降，餘部在嘉慶十九年初基本被殲滅或潰散，起義失敗。政治上，清廷贏得了這場對手，但代價是把直隸、山東、河南三省推入高壓的連坐與清查，督撫更替、官員被貶，教門轉入更深的地下，中央集權並未因此實質加強。象徵上，皇城之夜是清代宮禁史上最刺眼的一頁，此後清廷對宮門警衛與旗籍宿衛的整頓一直延續到道光朝，紫禁城曾被教匪攻入成為後世反覆援引的案例。更長遠的結果是，癸酉之變證明了兩個道理：一是秘密結社加上災荒的組合，在王朝中晚期仍有爆發力；二是靠團練平叛的辦法會把國家推向地方軍閥化的方向。這一點，要到太平天國之後才完全顯形，而那時的火繩式鳥槍與抬槍，依然是許多團練手上唯一的遠射武器。
resultEn: The result has military, political and symbolic layers. Militarily the rising was crushed within half a year: after Huaxian fell the first leader Li Wencheng died in the ruins, the strongholds at Caozhou and in Zhili were taken one by one or starved into surrender, and the remnants were destroyed or scattered by the beginning of 1814, so the revolt failed. Politically the court won the contest, but the price was to push Zhili, Shandong and Henan into a state of high-pressure collective investigation and purge, with viceroys replaced and officials demoted, and the cult driven further underground; the centralisation of the state did not in fact grow. Symbolically, that night at the palace is the most glaring page in the history of the Qing palace guards, and the reforms of the palace gates and of the banner watch that followed ran on into the Daoguang reign; the story of the Forbidden City having been entered by cult rebels became a stock example, cited again and again. In the longer run the rising demonstrated two things: that the combination of a secret sect with famine still had explosive force in the later middle period of the dynasty, and that suppressing rebellion with drill militia pushes the state towards the militarisation of the localities. That second point only became fully visible after the Taiping war, and by then the matchlock fowling piece and shoulder musket were still the only long arm many of the drill units possessed.
